sentences.text: This is the second round of litigation as far as the present Petitioner is concerned.

His main prayer is that he should be considered as a separate family unit for the purposes of re-settlement and rehabilitation as displaced person following the acquisition of land in Basudevpur for the purposes of Jindal Steel and Power Energy Limited in Angul district.

entities.text: Jindal Steel and Power Energy Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
2. Earlier, this writ petitioner had filed W.P.(C) No.2751 of 2014 which was disposed of on 24th June, 2014 by this Court directing the Revenue Divisional Commissioner (RDC), Northern Division,
Sambalpur to dispose of the Petitioner's representation and pass a reasoned order.

entities.text:
Revenue Divisional Commissioner (RDC), Northern Division,
Sambalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The RDC has since passed the impugned order dated 13th August, 2014 declining relief to the Petitioner.
3. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that the admitted date of birth of the Petitioner as per the transfer certificate issued by the school in which he studied is '10.4.1991'.

He refers to a circular dated 21st August, 1990 issued by the Department of Irrigation, according to which, the relevant date for determining rehabilitation benefits would be the date of the notification under Section 4 (1)
of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (LA Act).

According to the counsel for the Petitioner, since the notification under Section 4 (1) of the LA Act is dated 7th September 2009, going by that date the Petitioner would be a major and, therefore, would be entitled to be considered as a separate family unit for the purposes of the R & R Policy, 2006.

sentences.text: 1 4. Learned counsel for the Intervenor in Misc. Case No.10887 of 2015, i.e., Jindal Steel and Power Limited points out that the circular dated 21st August, 1990 issued by the Irrigation Department is not applicable as far as the project of the company concerned.
What is relevant is the Odisha Resettlement and Rehabilitation Policy, 2006.

Para 3 (c) of the said Policy defines "Cut-off date" and reads as under:
"3(c) Cut-off date for the purpose of compensation shall be the date on which the notification declaring the intention to acquire land under the relevant Act or under the provisions of this Policy is published.

Note: For the purpose of declaring eligibility for R & R benefits, the list of displaced families, will be updated on the 1st of January of the year in which the physical displacement is scheduled to take place provided that those families who move into the project area after determination of the "cut- off-date", will not be eligible for any benefit."

5. It is submitted that in the present case the uniform "Cut-off date"
declared was "1.1.2009".
As of that date the Petitioner was less than eighteen years by three months.
6. The above facts are not able to be disputed by the learned Counsel for the Petitioner.
He submits that since the Petitioner was short of the age of majority just by three months, a lenient view should be taken of the matter.
7. Once it is clear that the 2006 Policy that applies, the "Cut-off date" would have to be in terms of that Policy which in the present case is "1.1.2009".
Going by the date of birth of the Petitioner as disclosed by him, he would not have completed eighteen years as on "1.1.2009".
This is the reason that weighed with the RDC in rejecting his claim.
8. The Court is, accordingly, unable to find any error having been committee by the RDC in the impugned order.
9. There is no merit in the present writ petition and it is dismissed as such.

(Dr. S. Muralidhar) Chief Justice (M. S. Raman) Judge MRS/Laxmikant Tuna Bhoi vs State Of Odisha & Others .... Opposite ... on 12 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39107005/
